jhu-clsp/ettin-encoder-17m.note: Measured 2026-10-17 on the gate's own metric: budgeted patching, 512-byte axis, patch budget 128, batch 4, the gate's 64 held-out texts, 6000 Stage 1 steps on three Project Gutenberg books (data/pg84.txt, data/pg1342.txt, data/pg2701.txt), re-measured with scripts/measure_thresholds.py after centring was moved out of the per-batch loop and into the pooled evaluation set. Observed cos_emb_c 0.824, sim_corr 0.629, boundary_acc 0.949, trie coverage 1.00, raw cosine 0.994. Floors sit below those so a modestly worse rerun still ships, and far above a randomly initialised byte interface's cos 0.020 / sim_corr 0.073 / boundary 0.597 -- which exports cleanly and passes every check except these. The note previously recorded 0.841 / 0.717 / 0.944 for this model; those were measured with centring applied per batch, which made the same checkpoint score differently at batch 4 and at batch 16, and the metric now centres once over the whole evaluation set. The floors are unchanged because they remain below the re-measured values and far above the untrained ones. No other source model's floors may be borrowed for this one: fidelity numbers do not transfer between architectures, so a model that has never been gated is refused rather than guessed at.

hotchpotch/bekko-system-one-v0-17m.note: Measured 2026-10-17 with scripts/measure_thresholds.py on the gate's own metric: budgeted patching, 512-byte axis, patch budget 128, batch 4, the gate's 64 held-out texts, 6000 Stage 1 steps at lr 3e-4 on 4000 rendered Open-Jev decision queries and candidates (data/corpus/open-jev-train.jsonl, rendered by scripts/prepare_decision_corpus.py in the model's own instruction_state layout). Observed cos_emb_c 0.889, sim_corr 0.985, boundary_acc 0.996, trie coverage 1.00, raw cosine 0.989. Random-init contrast on the same texts: cos_emb_c 0.078, sim_corr 0.949, boundary_acc 0.671. Four things a reader of these floors must know. (1) sim_corr barely separates on this corpus: an untrained byte interface already reaches 0.949, because rendered decisions from one generator are homogeneous and almost any embedding reproduces their coarse cluster structure. The cos_emb_c and boundary_acc floors are what make this gate able to fail; the sim_corr floor of 0.97 is set above 0.949 and below 0.985 and should not be read as strong evidence. (2) This model is not published as an embedding model: it is a typed-decision model with three heads (choice, noul, score) over a shared-prefix encoder, resolving through a custom-code module layout (0_BekkoInference) rather than a plain checkpoint. What is byteified here is the shared encoder and its mean-pooled representation, which is what those heads read. (3) There is deliberately NO retrieval_recall_at_1 floor here, and byteify build refuses level 2 with judgements for this model as a result. Measured: on 2000 held-out Open-Jev decisions the SOURCE model scores recall@1 0.262 against a chance level of 0.419, because ranking candidates by cosine between mean-pooled embeddings is not how it decides. Three Stage 1 runs of one recipe scored 0.488, 0.301 and 0.281 on the same decisions, a spread wider than any margin a floor could be placed inside with confidence, and the level-2 contrastive stage does not close it -- scripts/contrastive_tradeoff.py measured seven rungs and none both held these fidelity floors and beat 0.45, and freezing the embedding tables preserved fidelity but left recall@1 at 0.287. A floor that half of identical runs fail is a coin flip dressed as a gate, so the number is left unpublished rather than guessed. (4) Fidelity numbers do not transfer between architectures, so no floor here may be borrowed for another source model.
